notes: Two quiet safeguards, and one honest nudge. First: what the assistant reads from disk can no longer leak out in a reply - every outbound message (Telegram, a channel, a cron job, a mission report, the console) is scanned for the shapes credentials actually have (sk- keys, github and slack tokens, AWS key ids, Azure account keys, connection-string passwords, private key blocks, bot tokens, JWTs) and the value is replaced by a mask that keeps the shape, so you still see that a credential was there while the secret itself never leaves the machine. The mask is output-side only: nothing the model reads is touched, and the shell keeps its declared trust boundary - we do not pretend bash is sandboxed. Second: the handful of command shapes that pipe a download straight into a privileged shell or wipe a system path are now refused with the reason and a pointer back to you; ordinary work (rm -rf ./build, cat /etc/hostname, curl | jq) still runs. Third, a one-line nudge on the Exchange panel when today's order activity is above your own trailing seven-day baseline - local facts only, nothing is blocked, reversed or reported anywhere. No new credential, no new outbound path, and the upgrade action stays one click in the console.
